tagline: Hosted website builder for portfolios, businesses, blogs, and stores.
verdictSummary: A personal portfolio-and-blog site — static pages generated from Markdown, a working contact form, an RSS feed — is a real weekend build with excellent performance by default. What doesn't come with it is Squarespace's actual product: a visual drag-and-drop editor, a large template library, and built-in e-commerce.
coreLoopDIY: A static site generated from Markdown content, with a shared layout system, a working contact form, and an RSS feed, deployed as plain files.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because it removes design, hosting, and maintenance from a website project entirely — not because a portfolio site is technically hard to build.
notes: A mainstream entry where the honest verdict genuinely depends on how much of the site's complexity is store-and-editor versus plain content.
prompt:
Build a personal website — home, about, a projects grid, and a blog — as a static site generated from Markdown content files with front matter for title, date, and tags. Use one shared layout system (a base template plus reusable partials for header, footer, and content cards) so a redesign touches one place, not every page. Generate blog tag pages and an RSS feed at build time. Add a working contact form that posts to a small server endpoint, emails you the message, and logs it as a fallback, with a honeypot field rather than a captcha. Build to plain static files, deployable to any static host or a small VPS behind a reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS.

Do not build a drag-and-drop editor, e-commerce, or switchable themes — editing Markdown and CSS directly is the trade for owning the whole thing outright.

faq.q: Can I export my existing Squarespace site?
faq.a: Squarespace offers limited content export, mainly blog posts in a WordPress-compatible format, which is a reasonable starting point — layout, design, and any store or booking pages need to be rebuilt from scratch.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The published site itself is fully responsive. Editing content means editing Markdown files, which is a desktop task, not a phone one — that's the trade against Squarespace's own mobile-friendly editor.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Static hosting is often free or a couple of dollars a month, plus a domain — genuinely cheap since there's no database or per-visit server work.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The visual editor. Every future layout change here means editing code and redeploying, not dragging a block around in a browser — a real, ongoing trade for a non-technical site owner.
